findings.source_quote: οὗ ἦσαν δένδρα καρπῶν πλήρη, ἄλλοις καὶ ἄλλοις καρποῖς κεκοσμημένα
findings.english_quote: The eleventh mountain had trees full of many different kinds of fruit.
findings.issue: The simplified sentence preserves fullness and variety but drops the separate description of the trees as adorned with fruit. This removes part of the source's visual imagery rather than merely shortening its syntax.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “The eleventh mountain had trees full of fruit, adorned with many different kinds of fruit.” Review this proposed wording against the source before adoption.

findings.source_quote: εἰ τὰ ἔθνη τοὺς δούλους αὐτῶν κολάζουσιν, ἐάν τις ἀρνήσηται τὸν κύριον ἑαυτοῦ, τί δοκεῖτε ποιήσει ὁ Κύριος ὑμῖν
findings.english_quote: The nations punish their servants if they deny their own master. What, then, do you think the Lord will do to you?
findings.issue: The outer conditional, “If the nations punish,” becomes an unqualified assertion about the nations. The inner condition concerning a servant's denial remains, but the source's conditional framing of the comparison does not.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “If the nations punish their servants when one denies their own master, what do you think the Lord will do to you?” Review the replacement independently before adoption.

summary: The standard edition faithfully represents the selected working Greek, including its difficult claims about suffering, sins, and life. Its notes accurately distinguish the relevant reported alternatives and editorial restoration without claiming fresh manuscript verification. The simplified edition independently preserves the principal teaching, negations, obligations, and speaker attribution, but needs two localized corrections to retain the adornment imagery and the conditional comparison. Acceptance here concerns the supplied text and attributed reports, not authentication of unseen manuscripts or exhaustive collation.
